opus-juror.first_action: I would tap the "A knight fights a three-headed hydra" suggestion card and then tap "Make it!".

losses.note: The game drops me straight into a fight with a small instruction banner ("Dodge the wind-up, strike in the opening"), and I can't see what a wind-up looks like or when the opening is.
I lost all 3 lives in 4.8 s with 1 point and 2% progress, so the difficulty feels punishing before I've learned anything.
The clear hint "Tap right to strike, tap left to dodge" only appears on the game-over screen, when it would have helped before the first hit.

opus-juror.verdict: I'd probably tap "Try again" once because getting from a sentence to a playable game in about 3 seconds is impressive, but dying in under 5 seconds with no real tutorial makes me likely to move on soon after.

opus-player.first_action: I'd tap the knight vs three-headed hydra card and then hit the big orange Make it! button.

losses.note: The game just drops me in with a line of text about wind-ups and openings, and I can't tell if I'm supposed to press the Dodge/Strike buttons or tap the screen, so I lose my lives figuring it out.

I died after 4.8s with 0 lives, 1 point and 2% progress, so it feels like it was over before I even knew how to play, and it only tells me 'tap right to strike, tap left to dodge' after I already lost.

There's a ton on screen at once (hearts, timer, instruction box, banner, Quick/Full detail toggle, two action buttons, Change one thing, share), so it's hard to tell where to look while the enemy is already coming.

opus-player.verdict: Probably yes, I'd hit Try again once since now I get the tap-left/tap-right controls and making my own game is kinda cool, but if I die that fast again I'd go back to TikTok.

codex-juror.first_action: I would enter a game idea in the text box and click “Make it!”.

losses.note: “Tap to play,” “Make it!” and the suggestion cards compete as starting points.

codex-juror.verdict: I would stop at 10 seconds because the game still appears to require starting and my inputs have not produced clear progress.

opus-juror.first_action: I'd hit the big yellow "Tap to play" button on the featured crystal game, since it's the most eye-catching thing on the page, or else type a sentence and press "Make it!".

losses.note: The main game preview is still an empty dark-navy box with only the caption and Tap to play, so at first glance it looks unloaded.

A knight and a hydra appear with a 'Beat the three-headed hydras!' banner, but nothing on screen says which keys or taps strike or dodge, and this hydra game has nothing to do with the fox prompt or the crystal preview.
Almost 5 seconds after the first accepted key press, the timer has reset to 0.0s and a 'Tap to start' overlay sits there with the scene unchanged, so my key presses seem to have done nothing.

opus-juror.verdict: Probably not: the say-a-sentence idea is clear and quick, but at 10 seconds I'm still staring at 'Tap to start' after pressing keys, so it feels stuck rather than playable.

opus-player.first_action: I'd hit the big yellow "Tap to play" button on the preview game, because it's the most obvious thing on the screen, before I'd bother typing anything.

losses.note: The main game area is just a dark navy box with text and a button, so for a second it looks like nothing loaded.
I'm dropped into a knight-vs-hydra fight with the timer already running at 1.4s and nothing tells me which keys to press.
After five seconds of pressing keys, a 'Tap to start' box pops up and the timer is back at 0.0s, so it feels like none of my presses counted and the game never really started.

opus-player.verdict: I'd probably quit around now, because making a game from one sentence is cool, but after 10 seconds I still haven't actually played and the controls only showed up after my button mashing seemed to do nothing.
